text:
riley: Customer on prod is seeing intermittent 5xx on POST /v1/generate, reported latency spikes and error. They provided a request_id: req_7b9f2c. Can someone pull server logs for that req and share what shard/host handled it?
riley: Customer says it happened around 2026-03-16T18:42:12Z (UTC). Asking for steps they can run too.
asha: on it — first pass: which region? (us-west-2?) also do we have the client's raw x-request-id header or only that request_id?
riley: They pasted the header: x-request-id: req_7b9f2c, x-client: customer-xyz. Region appears to be us-west-2 based on their account.
jace: quick Kibana/KQL I run locally to look across shards: 
```
@timestamp >= "2026-03-16T18:40:00Z" and @timestamp <= "2026-03-16T18:45:00Z" and labels.request_id : "req_7b9f2c"
```
This should hit hot storage. If not found, we need to check cold archive index pattern `logs-archive-*` with the same filter.
asha: note retention: hot logs (kibana) are kept ~14 days; archived indexes kept 90 days. If user waited >14d we'd need to kick off an archive rehydration request.
riley: customer said they saw it minutes ago so hot should have it.
ash a: ran query, nothing in hot for that request_id; scanning trace_id variants now. If still nothing I'll ask them for a curl repro so we can generate a live sample and attach debugbundle.
jace: also check proxy logs on the edge tier — sometimes request_id gets rewritten there. KQL for proxy: `service:edge AND message: "req_7b9f2c"`
sre-oncall: FYI if we need archived shard lookup I can run a direct ES shard search but need the index timeframe and a short maintenance window since it touches cold nodes.
riley: customer willing to run a curl — asked for exact command we want. Can we give them minimal repro that includes the x-request-id header?
jace: send them this (curl will hit prod endpoint):
```
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "x-request-id: req_7b9f2c" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-lite","input":"hello"}'
```
riley: pinging customer with that. Also asked them to capture the full response headers and body and paste the raw response.
asha: if they can reproduce, ask them to include `--trace-ascii /tmp/curl.trace` or `-v` output so we capture TLS handshake timing.
riley: customer ran the curl and pasted output — they got a 502 with body "upstream reset by peer". They also included `x-request-id` in response: req_7b9f2c.
jace: good, that confirms server saw it. I'll re-run KQL broadened to look for the trace id emitted by our edge: `labels.trace_id : * and labels.request_id : "req_7b9f2c"` and also a free-text search for "upstream reset"
jace: found a match in `prod-logs-2026.03.16` on host gpu-12-usw2, lines show kernel OOM killer spikes at same second. Copying snippet: "kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 33421 (infer-worker)" — opening infra ticket.
asha: if that's the case, we should mark this as service degradation and propose a short mitigation: move this customer to a different pool or enable automatic fallback to cpu-serve for this request pattern.
sre-oncall: I'll escalate to infra and request GC/oom logs from gpu-12-usw2. Also scheduling a short capacity increase.
riley: passing to customer: "We located the request in prod logs on host gpu-12-usw2 and see kernel OOM at the same timestamp which caused an upstream reset. We're escalating to infra. We'll follow up with mitigation steps and whether we need to replay any requests or refund tokens." :thumbsup:
asha: for our KB, KQL we used for final find: 
```
index: prod-logs-* AND @timestamp:["2026-03-16T18:41:30Z" TO "2026-03-16T18:43:00Z"] AND (message: "req_7b9f2c" OR message: "upstream reset" OR message: "Out of memory")
```
riley: thanks all. saving debug bundle instructions to the ticket: `curl -H "x-request-id: req_7b9f2c" ...` and ask them to attach stdout from the client and the curl trace.
kibana-bot: search completed for index pattern `prod-logs-*` — 1 hit found (doc id: prod-2026-03-16-00012345) — link: https://kibana.redwood.ai/app/discover#/doc/prod-logs-00012345
asha: closing loop — infra confirmed transient OOM on gpu-12-usw2; host was autoscaled down because of unrelated maintenance. Remediation: added preemptive buffer on that pool and enabled fallback route to `gpt-cpu-fallback`.
jace: adding note to ticket: how to hunt similar incidents: check edge rewrite, then lookup request_id across `prod-logs-*`, then `logs-archive-*` if not found, and check host-level kernel logs for OOM.
riley: customer updated: they retried 2x and succeeded on retry after ~30s. I told them we'll monitor and reached out with a credit offer. Closing thread after infra confirms host stabilized. :white_check_mark:
